summary.name: Luxury Editorial (category: Graphic Design and Design Movements; provenance explicit, directly named in the source).
summary.visualIdentity: The source explicitly directs one highlighted subject with refined display type, concise copy, generous space, selective image cropping and restrained color. Material highlights are used sparingly. Luxury must not be equated with excessive gold, sparkle or blur.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: the style is strongest alone with one subject and refined type. Source-named combination uses include fashion, hospitality, invitations, premium product reveals, lookbooks, property showcases and collection launches. Inferred: single-subject premium product or editorial introductions and restrained portfolio galleries.
summary.limitations: Explicit: do not substitute gold, sparkle or heavy blur for luxury, and avoid heavy depth blur. Cropping does not remove backgrounds, create cutouts or fill missing artwork, and only supplied imagery may be layered. Unspecified: duration, aspect ratio, resolution and frame rate are not style constraints. Two-color contrast checks do not prove readability over images, video or animated light.
summary.palette: Suggested, not supplied: background #F4EFE7 ivory is the dominant layout ground, foreground #29251F dark brown carries text and ink, and accent_1 #817159 muted taupe is decorative only. Foreground on background measures 13.308, meeting the 4.5 body-text target. Accent on background measures 4.132, failing it, so accent must not carry body text. No gradient is enabled. Task-supplied exact colors override these tokens, and assets must not be recolored.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit guidance calls for smooth camera moves, subtle parallax and precise settling, with limited parallax and slow moves. Shared guidance avoids automatic springs, bounce or extra in-between poses, and preserves deliberate cuts and reading holds. Optional candidates motion-012, -013, -015, -018 and -038 apply only when scene content supports them. Motion-038 needs an actual punctuation mark. Video state derives from composition time; scroll and swipe are interactive-only.
summary.audio: Unspecified: the source gives no audio requirement, so audio must be proposed per task and stated as an assumption. Inferred: restrained ambience or silence suits a premium, reading-paced mood and leaves room for narration. Music should not compete with speech or essential text. Music-synchronized timing is valid only after real audio analysis. Gallery previews remain silent.
summary.assetRequirements: Supplied or authorized imagery is required, since the source never assumes photographic assets exist. Local fonts should be loaded for refined display type, with measured spacing. Exact copy and brand names must be supplied; do not invent product copy or brand marks. Crops need generous negative space for type while keeping faces, product details and original color treatment intact. Punctuation Zoom needs an actual glyph or approved mark.
summary.combinations: The source says Luxury Editorial is strongest alone and should be hybridized only for tactile title moments or measured depth. Optional style-052 adds shallow debossed letterpress for title cards only, with #29251F ink and #817159 for one rule or monogram. Avoid metallic bevels, gold gradients and paper texture on every scene. Optional style-101 adds 2.5D parallax across cropped layers with one slow ease-out move per scene. Avoid heavy blur, multi-axis parallax and exposed layer edges.
summary.productionApproach: Style renderer: HTML/CSS for real typography, grid layout and clip-path, plus SVG for masks and strokes. Motion engine: a GSAP paused timeline with one owner per animated property; Motion is optional and needs explicit synchronization. HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for check, snapshot and render; Remotion is a fallback only with a recorded reason. chroma-js validates colors, Cropper.js prepares crops, and PhotoSwipe serves only interactive galleries. Verify forward, backward and direct seeks plus composited frames.
